chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Abd Allah ibn Muskān said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Nāsibī (one known for enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt) whose enmity is known. Can the believer marry him, while he is capable of repelling him, and he does not know of the repulsion? He said: The believer does not marry the Nāsibīyah, nor does the Nāsibī marry a believing woman, nor does the weak believer marry a believing woman.

key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: Nāsibī, one known for enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a Nāsibī in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar outlines the prohibition of intermarriage between believers and the Nāsibī (those known for enmity towards the Ahl al-Bayt), emphasizing that the believer must not marry a Nāsibī, nor should a Nāsibī marry a believing woman. It further extends this ruling to the 'Mustaḍʿaf' (the weak or less steadfast believer), prohibiting them from marrying a believing woman to prevent religious dilution or influence. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of 'al-Walāʾ wa al-Barāʾ' (loyalty and disavowal) in personal and familial relations.
